subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Differential Gears: Splitting Power
description: A fast breakdown of Differential Gears: Splitting Power for builders.

hook.text: In a turn, the outer wheel travels farther than the inner one. The differential lets them spin at different speeds.

buildup.text: A ring gear drives a carrier holding small spider gears. The spider gears allow each axle to rotate independently.

discovery.text: Going straight, both axles turn together. In a curve, spider gears rotate — one axle speeds up, the other slows down.

twist.text: On ice, a standard differential sends all power to the spinning wheel. Limited-slip differentials fix this flaw.

climax.text: Every car with two driven wheels needs a differential. Without it, tires would scrub and axles would snap in turns.

punchline.text: Split the power. Let each wheel find its own speed.

quiz.question: What problem does a limited-slip differential solve?
options: It reduces noise from the differential gears during cornering
It prevents all power from going to a spinning wheel on slippery surfaces
It allows the car to reverse direction without changing gears
